gotchas.note: Revenue and expenses by team are only in sports (one row per sponsored sport). For a school's men's vs. women's spending, sum sports.expense_menall / expense_womenall, or use v_spending_by_gender. Team figures leave out money not assigned to any team (institutions.tot_expense_all_notalloc: facilities, administration...); grnd_total_expense = all team expenses + not allocated. Say which one a number is.

gotchas.topic: EADA leaves out capital, debt service and indirect facilities
gotchas.note: Per the Department of Education's EADA User's Guide (Sept 2026, Total Expenses and Total Revenues instructions), schools must not report capital expenditures, debt service, or indirect facilities support (facilities and services the institution provides but doesn't charge to athletics) as expenses or revenues. So EADA totals are lower than, and not comparable to, the 'total athletics spending' in NCAA financial reports or news stories, which include those. Say 'operating spending as reported to EADA' and don't reconcile the two. The instructions for earlier survey years were not checked and may be worded differently.

sports.partic_* and sum_partic_* count an athlete once per team, so summing them over sports counts multi-sport athletes several times (participation opportunities, not people). For people (proportionality, per-athlete spending) use institutions.undup_ct_partic_men / undup_ct_partic_women, as v_proportionality does.

Columns ending in _menall / _womenall, sum_partic_* and the unduplicated counts INCLUDE co-ed team members of that sex; partic_men / partic_women do not. Say whether a figure includes co-ed teams when it matters.

Use v_proportionality: female share of full-time undergraduates minus female share of (unduplicated) athletes, in percentage points. Positive = women underrepresented among athletes. Prong 1 of the three-part test only; it does not establish compliance or non-compliance.
efmalecount / effemalecount / eftotalcount are FULL-TIME UNDERGRADUATES (what EADA reports under 20 U.S.C. 1092(g)), not total enrollment. eftotalcount = efmalecount + effemalecount.
Names are official IPEDS names (e.g. 'The University of Alabama'). Resolve user wording through institution_aliases (ILIKE), then filter on unitid.

survey_year is the END of the academic year: 2025 = 2024-25. Loaded 2016-2025. 2021 (2020-21, COVID) has ~200 fewer schools; don't call a 2020-to-2021 drop a trend. The latest year predates revenue sharing (2025-26).
About 61% of school-years report total revenue exactly equal to expenses (institutional support fills the gap), so revenue minus expenses is not a measure of profit or of which teams 'make money'.

sports has only sponsored sports (rows with no participants were dropped at build time; the raw 2019-20 file listed unsponsored ones). A missing school+sport row = not sponsored. partic_men / partic_women are NULL when that sport has no team of that sex; money and coach columns are 0 instead. Count women's teams with partic_women IS NOT NULL.

Filter on sports after get_enum_values. Track and swimming are reported combined ('Track and Field and Cross Country (combined)', 'Swimming and Diving (combined)') or split, depending on the school: include both forms. 'Other Sports' lumps unlisted sports.
EADA has no conference column. classification_name gives the division (e.g. 'NCAA Division I-FBS'); some values have trailing spaces, so use TRIM or ILIKE.

sports has coach counts by team gender x coach sex (e.g. women_team_head_coaches_female), full- and part-time combined. Salaries are only per school, as averages: *_salary_* per coach, *_sal_fte_* per full-time equivalent (fairer when part-time coaches differ by team gender). num_hdcoach_* (per school) differs from the sum of sport-level head coaches in ~2% of school-years.

EADA records institutional athletics money. Third-party NIL deals never appear here, and revenue-sharing payments are not in the years loaded. Use nil_facts for NIL figures and say which money flow each number belongs to.
